title: Two Killed, Indian Seafarer Injured as Russian Drone Sinks Turkish Cargo Ship
excerpt: A Russian drone strike set fire to the Turkish-owned cargo vessel Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea, killing the captain and one other crew member. Three Indian nationals were aboard; one was injured and is receiving treatment in Romania.
body:
• Two crew members were killed and 11 rescued after the Turkish-owned cargo ship Royad Mammadov caught fire and sank in the Black Sea on Monday, about 30 nautical miles south of Romania's Sfantu Gheorghe. Ukraine says two Russian drones struck the vessel.
  • Three Indian nationals were among the crew; one was injured and is receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital in Romania. Ambassador Manoj Mohapatra confirmed all three are in good health and receiving necessary care.
  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the ship was carrying corn in neutral waters and that its captain was killed. Romania's interior ministry has not confirmed the cause of the fire.
  • The St Kitts & Nevis-flagged vessel had departed Ukraine's Izmail port bound for Italy. Turkey's Chamber of Maritime Commerce says 226 civilian and commercial vessels have been attacked in the Black Sea since the war began, most of them this year.

Two crew members were killed and an Indian seafarer was among several injured after a Russian drone strike set fire to a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Monday, in one of the deadliest attacks on commercial shipping since the war began. The 139-metre general cargo ship Royad Mammadov caught fire inside Romania's exclusive economic zone, about 30 nautical miles south of Sfantu Gheorghe, and later sank. Eleven of the 13 people aboard were rescued; the injured were airlifted by helicopter to hospitals in Romania.

Context & Background

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia directly, describing "a horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Türkiye." He said Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were aboard, the ship's captain was killed, and the fate of one other person was still being established at the time of his statement.

""Pressure is needed to restore global food security."

Romania's interior ministry said its Coast Guard was alerted at around 11 am local time but did not confirm the cause of the fire; Romanian media reported the vessel was hit by a drone southeast of a Black Sea oil platform. Russia had no immediate comment, though its defence ministry said in a daily bulletin it had struck two cargo vessels, according to AFP. The Royad Mammadov, flagged to Saint Kitts and Nevis, had departed Ukraine's Danube port of Izmail and was headed for Ravenna, Italy, vessel-tracking data showed.

Grain shipments from Ukraine's Danube ports have become the backbone of the country's wartime exports since Russia withdrew from the Black Sea grain initiative in 2023. Commercial vessels using the corridor have faced repeated attack, and the Black Sea has become an active battlefield for drone warfare more than four years into the invasion.

Impact & Analysis

The strike intensifies pressure on Black Sea shipping at a moment when Turkey — which brokered the original grain corridor and remains NATO's key Black Sea power — has grown openly frustrated. Turkey's Chamber of Maritime Commerce said last month that 226 civilian and commercial vessels have been attacked in the Black Sea since the war began, the vast majority this year. Turkish seafarers have staged protests over deaths suffered in the attacks, and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told the UN General Assembly the strikes were "unacceptable."

Zelenskyy used the attack to press for renewed international pressure to protect food shipments. "Pressure is needed to restore global food security. And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help," he posted. For insurers, shipowners and crewing agencies, Monday's sinking is a reminder that the Black Sea remains an active conflict zone for civilian shipping — with the cost measured in crew lives, not just hulls and cargo.

Diaspora Angle

India supplies a large share of the world's merchant seafarers, and Indian crew routinely serve aboard foreign-flagged cargo ships passing through the Black Sea. Monday's attack put Indian nationals in harm's way — a day after a 52-year-old employee of an Indian-owned pharmaceutical warehouse was killed in a Russian strike in Ukraine's Sumy region. The Indian Embassy in Romania said it was in close contact with authorities on the safety and welfare of the three Indian crew members, while external affairs minister S. Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy to active engagement with both Kyiv and Moscow on resolving the conflict.

What's Next

The injured crew are being treated at Constanța County Hospital, and Romanian authorities are expected to release a fuller accounting of the casualties. Whether Turkey escalates its response — Ankara has protested to both sides over earlier attacks — and whether the sinking prompts fresh insurance or routing changes for Black Sea grain traffic are the key questions to watch. India is likely to raise the safety of its nationals with both capitals as Jaishankar's engagement with Kyiv and Moscow continues.
